title: Read the JIT settings from a java command line

blocks.text: HotSpot's JIT is steered by `-XX` flags: `-XX:+Name` turns a boolean on, **`-XX:-Name` turns it off**, and `-XX:Name=value` sets a number. When a flag appears more than once, **the last one wins**.
Write `JitFlags.parse(args)` for these flags, ignoring every other argument:

The result answers `tiered()`, `topTier()`, `maxInlineSize()`, `freqInlineSize()`, `printCompilation()` and `printInlining()`. `topTier()` is the stop level when tiered compilation is on, and 4 (C2 alone) when it is off.
A stop level outside 0 to 4 is refused with `IllegalArgumentException`, and so is `PrintInlining` turned on **without `-XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions`**.

rows: tiered, top tier 4, inline sizes 35 and 325

cases.says: With no JIT flags the defaults hold (tiered, top tier 4, inline sizes 35 and 325); given flags change them and unrelated flags such as -Xmx4g are ignored.
-XX:-TieredCompilation turns tiered compilation off, leaving C2 alone at tier 4, even when a stop level is also given.
When a flag appears twice, the later value is the one that counts.
TieredStopAtLevel accepts 0 (interpreter only) through 4 and refuses anything else with IllegalArgumentException.
PrintInlining is refused with IllegalArgumentException unless -XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions is also given; -XX:-UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions does not unlock it.

concepts: PrintCompilation shows what is compiled, and PrintInlining is a diagnostic flag that needs UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions.
Tiered compilation starts in the interpreter, compiles hot methods with C1 while profiling and recompiles the hottest with C2, and -XX:-TieredCompilation or TieredStopAtLevel change that path.
